newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Bank of Namibia to lift forex controls this year.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Namibia to lift forex controls this year.

text.p: The Bank of Namibia this year will lift most remaining foreign exchange controls on capital and current account transactions, according to its annual report, released on Wednesday.
"The remaining exchange controls, on both current and capital transactions, will be phased out gradually during the year," the bank said.

"While this could result in capital outflows that would put further pressure on foreign reserves and the balance of payments, virtually all remaining current account restrictions will be abolished," it added.

Namibia recorded a balance of payments surplus of N$98 million, or 0.7 percent of gross domestic product in 1996, about the same as in 1995. The surplus reflected strong export earnings and an increase in transfers from the Southern African Customs Union (SACU).
However, such transfers were expected to decline with trade liberalisation. "This underlines the importance of promoting an export-biased production," the bank said.

The bank said its commitment to abolishing foreign exchange restrictions was underscored by its accession to Article V111 of the International Monetary Fund. The article precludes member countries from imposing restrictions on payments and transfers for current international transactions, or from engaging in discriminatory currency arrangements without IMF approval.

Namibia has already started divesting more authority to authorised dealers. It has formulated policies to allow foreign-controlled companies to borrow on the domestic market, and approved direct corporate investment in countries outside the Common Monetary Area.
Further requests by Namibian institutional investors to invest abroad are now sanctioned by the bank. It has also introduced policies to offset foreign liabilities against foreign accruals.
